name: English
tagline: Two songs in, one alloy out.
subtitle: An open-source desktop studio for rule-based auto-mashups, slowed + reverb and lofi, with a real timeline editor.
demo_caption: Intro, import, automatic analysis, Forge, a sequential mix, one-click Slowed + Reverb, export.
f_d: Pick two or more songs. Auralloy matches tempo and key, then plays them one after another, beat-matched, with a smooth blend at every switch.
Every decision follows a written rule and is logged in plain language. No black box.
Multi-track timeline with snapping, split, trim, fades, reverse, per-clip gain, tempo and pitch, loop regions and unlimited undo.
One-click looks and a full effects rack: EQ, lofi tape, compressor, chorus, echo, reverb, width, rain and vinyl.
WAV 16/24/32-bit float, FLAC and MP3 at 44.1 to 96 kHz, processed in 32-bit float.
AGPL-3.0, headless tests, a seeded benchmark suite and a research preprint.
how: Analyse tempo, beats, bars, key and sections.
Split stems: vocals, drums, bass, other.
Plan the arrangement with the mashup rules and write the log.
Render every clip with matched tempo and pitch.
Edit: everything is an ordinary clip on the timeline.
start: Drop two or more songs into the window.
Open Forge and press the orb: the songs play one after another.
Edit on the timeline, pick a look, then Export.
rules_intro: Forge follows explicit rules and writes a plain-language log of every decision.
rules: One shared tempo, with the least time-stretching.
One shared key (A minor equals C major), with the smallest pitch shift.
Every cut on a downbeat, in 4-bar phrases.
One vocal and one bass at a time; the bass swaps on a bar line.
Sections matched by energy; blends of 2 to 8 bars.
Every song keeps its own balance and is level-matched.
tour: Studio: song ribbon, role lanes, effects rack.
Forge: decks, compatibility matrix and the plan.
Export: WAV, FLAC, MP3, normalise, dither.
bench_intro: Seeded, synthetic and reproducible (see benchmarks/). Real music will be messier.
limits: Quick Stems is classic DSP, not a neural separator.
Key detection can be wrong on ambiguous harmony.
Validated on synthetic songs; real music needs more testing.
paper: A research preprint describing the method and its evaluation is published on Zenodo. It has not been peer reviewed.
rights: Auralloy is a tool: you are responsible for the rights to the audio you import.
more: Build instructions, shortcuts and technical docs are in the English README.
